newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet continues to trade higher.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet continues to trade higher.

text.p: Singapore jet fuel traded 40 cents higher on Wednesday from a day earlier as a local trader continued to price out its cargo sales to Indonesia, traders said.
The trader bought a 100,000-barrel lot from a European major at $29.50 per barrel for March 20-24 lifting fob, which was about $3.50 above gas oil values.
A Western trader was offering a larger cargo of 240,000 barrels for March 31-April 4 lifting at $28.55 fob, which did not meet the timing required by buyers.

Traders said physical jet fuel prices were currently overpriced, and they believed that a realistic spread with gas oil should be around $2.00 per barrel, which is about the current level seen in the March swaps market.

Gas oil was also strong with the same trader buying 220,000 barrels from a European major at $25.95 per barrel for March 23-27 lifting fob. A bid was later seen at $26.15 for 250,000 barrels for March 22-26 lifting fob.
However a European major bid at a lower level of $25.50 per barrel.

Traders said the strong gas oil market was continuing to attract arbitrage cargoes from Europe and the Mediterranean with 250,000-300,000 tonnes said to have already been fixed to Asia for end-March/early April delivery.
But one trader said the volume that would actually arrive this way would be around 160,000 tonnes, "at the most."
Nevertheless, some traders fear that when all these cargoes arrive in Asia, the gas oil market would be bound for a downward correction.

However, the extent of the fall could be cushioned by several turnarounds and refinery problems in Asia despite soft regional demand. South Korean refiners, that have been a major regional supplier recently with about seven export cargoes each month, would start their turnaround season in April, peaking in May.
